name: Glimmer.js (@glimmer/compiler)
recipe: npm pack @glimmer/compiler@0.94.11 + its pure-JS deps (@glimmer/syntax, @glimmer/util, @glimmer/wire-format, @glimmer/interfaces, @handlebars/parser, simple-html-tokenizer). esbuild --bundle --format=esm --platform=neutral into one self-contained .mjs exposing precompile(). Run that bundle on the already-LIVE qjs (QuickJS) sandbox. No native addons, no node-gyp, no install scripts, no fs/process/DOM/WASM in dist (verified via grep over package/dist). precompile is a pure function: template string in, wire-format JSON string out. Runtime VM (@glimmer/runtime) is DOM-bound and out of scope — only the compiler runs in-sandbox, which matches the item's claim.
smoke:
In qjs, import the esbuild bundle and run: precompile('
{{name}}
') — expect a JSON string wire-format block (e.g. contains "block":"[[...]]","moduleName") and no thrown error / no DOM reference.
blocker: Only the compiler is sandbox-viable; the @glimmer/runtime VM needs a real/host DOM (no GPU, but DOM-bound) so live rendering is out of scope. ESM bundling step required (esbuild) since package ships only ESM with @glimmer/* sub-imports — must be flattened for qjs.

name: Bison
recipe: Bison is self-contained C (Lane B on the surface: C + libc, no JIT/codegen, pure file-in/file-out grammar->C-tables transform). BLOCKER is architectural: the bison driver expands its skeleton files (data/*.m4) by fork/exec-ing GNU m4 as a SEPARATE subprocess at runtime (lib/spawn-pipe + m4sugar invocation via pipe/fork/execvp). wasm32-wasi under wasmtime has no fork/exec/subprocess spawning, so the unmodified program cannot run. m4 alone is itself Lane-B-buildable and would be live-likely standalone, but bison-the-tool hard-depends on spawning it out-of-process. Making it work needs non-trivial source surgery (link m4 expansion in-process / replace the spawn-pipe call), which is beyond a drop-in self-contained build, so no clean lane as-is.
blocker: bison fork/exec's GNU m4 as a separate process at runtime to expand skeleton (.m4) files; wasm32-wasi/wasmtime has no fork/exec/subprocess support, so the unmodified tool cannot run in-sandbox.

name: Flex
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C). Use the release tarball flex-2.6.4.tar.gz, which ships PREGENERATED scan.c (built by the bundled flex), so no lex bootstrap is needed. Compile the C sources (src/*.c) against our C/libc lane — :include_only amalgam style, no autotools/configure (provide a hand-written config.h with HAVE_* defines for wasi). Pure-function transform: reads a .l spec on stdin/file, writes C scanner source to stdout. No JIT, no GPU, no network, no threads. BLOCKER to resolve: flex's runtime emits the scanner by shelling out to an external `m4` binary (execvp of M4 over flex.skl skeleton) — wasi-preview1 under wasmtime has no process spawn, so a naive build aborts at runtime. Resolution paths: (a) build flex's `--with-m4` / internal skeleton path so the skeleton is preprocessed at BUILD time and the table-driven scan emitted without a runtime m4 exec — flex >=2.6 can be configured to bake the skeleton (flex.skl -> skel.c) at build time, eliminating the exec; verify M4 is not invoked on the generation path; OR (b) link an m4.wasm and route the exec through our host exec broker if available. Path (a) is the in-sandbox-pure route.
blocker: Flex's scanner-generation path shells out to an external `m4` binary (execvp over flex.skl); wasi-preview1/wasmtime has no process spawn, so a default build aborts at runtime with "can't open m4" / exec failure. Compiles fine via the C lane (pregenerated scan.c, no lex bootstrap), but RUNNING requires either configuring flex to bake the m4 skeleton at build time (skel.c, no runtime exec) or providing an m4.wasm via a host exec broker. Whether build-time skeleton baking fully eliminates the m4 exec on every codepath is unverified — hence uncertain, not live-likely.

name: thrift
recipe: N/A — would be lane B (self-contained C++ via clang.wasm + libc++, pure IDL->source transform, no JIT/exec/net). BLOCKED: compiler/cpp builds its lexer/parser from flex source (thriftl.ll) and bison grammar (thrifty.yy) at build time via find_package(FLEX/BISON REQUIRED). No pregenerated parser .cc/.h is checked into the repo, so the build cannot proceed with clang alone — it needs flex.wasm + bison.wasm in the sandbox, which we do not provision. This violates lane B's 'no codegen unless pregenerated' rule.
smoke: echo 'struct Point { 1: i32 x; 2: i32 y; }' > test.thrift && wasmtime thrift.wasm --gen cpp -out . test.thrift && test -f Point.thrift.does-not-exist || ls -1 *.h *.cpp  # expect generated gen-cpp sources (test_types.h/.cpp) for the IDL
blocker: Compiler requires flex + bison codegen at build time (thriftl.ll / thrifty.yy → lexer/parser .cc); no pregenerated parser is checked into the repo and we don't provision flex.wasm/bison.wasm. Without the generated lexer/parser, clang+libc++ alone cannot build the thrift binary. Pure-transform/no-exec is fine; the blocker is purely the build-time codegen dependency.

name: wasmi
recipe: N/A — no buildable lane. Wasmi requires Rust 1.86 + edition 2024 (workspace Cargo.toml: rust-version="1.86", edition="2024"). Our only Rust path is mrustc ~1.74 (edition 2021 max), so Lane C is impossible: edition-2024 syntax/features are unparseable by mrustc, and the workspace is large (collections/core/ir/wasmi/wasmparser ^0.228 + a c_api proc-macro). No published plain wasm32-wasi .wasm CLI artifact (it's an embedder library, not a distributed CLI), so no Lane A. Not C/C++ (B) or Python/JS (D).
smoke: If it ever built: pipe a tiny .wat (e.g. (module (func (export "add") (param i32 i32)(result i32) local.get 0 local.get 1 i32.add)) into the wasmi CLI and assert add(2,3)=5. Runtime semantics are fine in-sandbox — wasmi is a pure-Rust register-machine interpreter with no JIT/native codegen and no_std support, so running it inside a wasm32-wasi guest under wasmtime is sound. The blocker is purely build-time.
blocker: Build infeasible: requires Rust 1.86 + edition 2024; mrustc caps at ~1.74/edition-2021 (cannot parse edition 2024). Large multi-crate workspace + a c_api proc-macro compound it. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi CLI .wasm exists (library/embedder, not a distributed CLI). Interpreter runtime itself is sandbox-safe; the wall is the toolchain, not execution semantics.

name: Tcl interpreter
recipe: Lane B (self-contained C, our clang+libc wasi-sdk lane — same path as the already-LIVE ruby/php/lua). Fetch the Tcl core source tarball from core.tcl-lang.org (ships a pregenerated autoconf `configure` — no autoreconf needed, configure is patchable per our :include_only/pregen stance). Configure with CC=clang --target=wasm32-wasi --sysroot=<wasi-sysroot>, `--disable-threads` (no pthreads → use the select()-based single-thread notifier), `--disable-shared` (static link), `--disable-load` (no dlopen in wasm). Tcl is a pure bytecode/tree interpreter in portable C with NO codegen/JIT, so nothing to lose under wasm. Stub or accept failure on the Unix OS commands WASI can't back: `socket`/`exec`/fork/`pipe`/signals (no sockets, no process spawn in wasip1) — these `error` at runtime, the core stays sound. `clock`/`select`/file I/O on WASI preopened dirs work. Link a tiny tclAppInit shell main() that drops into the interpreter. Output: standalone `tcl.wasm` run under wasmtime, scripts/stdin via preopen + stdio. NOT the wacl port (that's Emscripten/JS-pair: `-s WASM=1` + .data/.js glue + ::wacl::jscall — excluded).
smoke: echo 'puts [expr {2+2}]; puts [string toupper hello]; puts [lsort {3 1 2}]' | wasmtime tcl.wasm  →  expect 4 / HELLO / 1 2 3
blocker: No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists today — only an Emscripten/JS-pair port (wacl), which is excluded. Requires a fresh wasi-sdk port (config flags above). Unix-specific commands (socket/exec/fork/pipe/signals) are unbackable under wasip1 and will error at runtime, but the core interpreter (expr, string/list/dict, procs, file I/O on preopened dirs) is fully functional. Comparable effort/scope to ruby/php/lua, all already LIVE via this same C lane.

name: yq
recipe: No viable lane. yq is a Go program (github.com/mikefarah/yq). Runtime shape is ideal (pure stdin->stdout filter, no net/server/GPU), but Go does not map to any of our four lanes: A=prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi (verified absent — `gh api repos/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest` lists only native arch binaries: darwin/linux/freebsd/netbsd/openbsd/windows on amd64/arm64/386/mips/ppc/riscv/s390x — zero .wasm/wasi asset); B=C/C++ (N/A, Go); C=Rust via mrustc (N/A, Go); D=pure-Python/JS (N/A). Go-to-wasm32-wasi needs TinyGo (or Go 1.24 GOOS=wasip1, but stdlib Go emits a host-Go-runtime wasm, not a clean wasm32-wasi module our wasmtime command lane ingests; TinyGo for a program of yq's size — yaml.v3 + reflection-heavy expression evaluator — is non-trivial and outside our compiler set). No standalone wasm32-wasi build of yq exists upstream.
smoke: N/A — not buildable in our lanes. (If a wasm existed: `echo 'a: {b: [1,2,3]}' | wasmtime yq.wasm -- '.a.b[1]'` should print `2`.) For the underlying need, jq is already LIVE and handles JSON; YAML-specific filtering is the only gap yq would add.
blocker: Written in Go — no lane covers Go (TinyGo/Go-wasip1 not in our toolchain; mrustc is Rust-only, B is C/C++-only). No upstream wasm32-wasi asset exists (release assets are native-arch only). Adjacent jq already LIVE covers JSON filtering.

name: htmlq
recipe: Lane C (bare Rust via mrustc ~1.74). htmlq 0.5.0 deps: kuchikiki 0.8, html5ever 0.26, clap 4.5 (derive), lazy_static, url 2.2. Pure-function: reads HTML from stdin or -f file, runs CSS selectors, writes selected nodes/text/attrs to stdout or -o file. No network, no threads, no GPU. Sandbox-clean. BUT the dependency stack is proc-macro-heavy and codegen-heavy: clap derive (#[derive(Parser)]), html5ever's match_token! proc-macros, markup5ever/string_cache + phf build-script codegen. This is the large/proc-macro class mrustc cannot handle. No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi artifact published (crates.io ships native binaries only) so Lane A unavailable. Not C/C++ (B) or Python/JS (D). Would need: either (a) full cargo+rustc wasm32-wasi cross-compile outside the mrustc lane, or (b) mrustc gaining proc-macro+codegen support for this stack.
smoke:
printf '
  • X
  • Y
' | htmlq '.a' --text → expect: X
blocker: Rust lane is mrustc ~1.74, which cannot build the proc-macro/codegen-heavy dep stack (clap 4.5 derive, html5ever 0.26 match_token! macros, markup5ever/string_cache/phf build-script codegen). The program itself is fully sandbox-safe (pure HTML-in/nodes-out, stdin/stdout/file only, zero OS/net/GPU), and would run as plain wasm32-wasi if compiled with stock cargo+rustc — but no prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact exists and our live lane can't compile it. Resolvable only by adding a real rustc wasm32-wasi cross-compile path or extending mrustc proc-macro support.

name: Eigen
recipe: Lane B :include_only. Eigen is a header-only C++ template library (verified: Eigen/Dense is just #includes of Core/LU/Cholesky/QR/SVD/Geometry/Eigenvalues). No configure/codegen/CMake needed to USE it; CMake is only for installing/tests. No BLAS — Eigen ships its own kernels. No JIT, no threads required (single-threaded by default; OpenMP optional and omittable), no GPU, no network. Needs C++14, satisfied by our C++/libc++ toolchain. Vectorize off (-DEIGEN_DONT_VECTORIZE or just rely on scalar path; no wasm SIMD intrinsics needed). Drop the Eigen/ headers in the sandbox include root as an :include_only amalgam, then compile+run a user .cpp TU under clang.wasm -> wasm32-wasi -> wasmtime. NOTE the canonical home moved off eigen.tuxfamily.org (dead, ECONNREFUSED) to gitlab.com/libeigen/eigen — use that for header fetch.

name: Perl
recipe: No blessed prebuilt perl.wasm exists. Use the zeroperl project (perl5 compiled to wasm32-wasi via the clang lane with ASYNCIFY-lowered setjmp/longjmp). Build from 6over3/zeroperl (mirror: uswriting/zeroperl) — its CI emits `zeroperl.wasm`, a self-contained WASI reactor module (~9MB) that bundles the Perl interpreter + libs under perl-wasi-prefix/. Critically the default build uses ASYNCIFY (not the wasm exnref exception-handling proposal), so the output needs NO exception-handling support and runs on stock wasmtime — the exnref blocker in the original Substack write-up only applied to the `-mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj` path, which the current repo's ASYNCIFY default avoids. Integration: register `zeroperl.wasm` as the command module; first argv MUST be `zeroperl`; map /dev/null as a preopen depending on runtime. (wasmtime since v3.0/late-2025 also supports real EH, but ASYNCIFY path doesn't need it.)
smoke:
wasmtime run --dir=. zeroperl.wasm zeroperl -e 'print "hi
"; print uc("text"), "
"; my $s="a1b2c3"; $s =~ s/\d//g; print "$s
";' → expect: hi / TEXT / abc. Confirms interpreter init, string/regex (s///), STDOUT all work in-sandbox.
blocker: No published release artifact ("No releases published") — must build zeroperl from source (clang lane + ASYNCIFY) to get zeroperl.wasm; not a drop-in download. ASYNCIFY-reactor-on-wasmtime is inferred from the build config (zeroperl.wasm = reactor with asyncify, which lowers sjlj to plain wasm without exnref), not independently smoke-verified in sources.

name: Common Lisp
recipe: No viable recipe. SBCL (the reference impl) is a native-code compiler that emits machine code at runtime — JIT-shaped, fails jitless under wasmtime → impossible. ECL (bytecode interpreter, the non-JIT path) is the only candidate, but its only WASM target is emscripten-based: the build emits JS-glue imports (invoke_iii, emscripten setjmp emulation) and is documented to fail under non-emscripten runtimes (wasmedge/wasmtime produce "unknown import" errors). ECL's own author states the WASI port "is not ready yet." So there is no prebuilt PLAIN wasm32-wasi .wasm (Lane A fails — emscripten/JS-pair), and ECL is not self-contained C buildable for wasi (needs emscripten libc shims + setjmp glue, not pure C amalgam; Lane B fails). No bare Rust CL crate (Lane C) and not pure-Python/JS (Lane D).
smoke: N/A — no buildable wasm32-wasi artifact. (Intended smoke would be: echo '(format t "~a~%" (+ 1 2))' | wasmtime ecl.wasm — but no such jitless WASI binary exists.)
blocker: SBCL = runtime native-code JIT (no jitless wasm). ECL = only WASM target is emscripten (JS-glue imports invoke_iii + setjmp emulation), documented to fail under wasmtime/wasmedge; ECL's WASI port explicitly "not ready yet." No plain wasm32-wasi standalone build, no C-amalgam path, no Rust crate.

name: COBOL
recipe: GnuCOBOL is the only portable COBOL impl (mainframe IBM Enterprise COBOL with EBCDIC/CICS/DB2/JCL is a separate dialect, out of scope). cobc transpiles COBOL to C, which would feed our existing clang.wasm lane (Lane B compilable in principle). But running needs the libcob runtime, which is NOT a self-contained amalgam: (1) hard dependency on GMP/libgmp for COBOL packed-decimal and large-integer arithmetic, and GMP ships hand-written x86/arm asm plus an autoconf build, not trivially wasm32-wasi; (2) libcob itself is a multi-file C library built via autotools configure, no pregenerated amalgam; (3) ncurses needed for SCREEN SECTION, optional, can stub. Path: build the pure-C mini-gmp variant for wasi, build libcob C sources against it, then transpile+compile user COBOL via cobc to C to clang.wasm. cobc itself also links libcob and must run in-sandbox or be pre-run on host to emit C. Feasible but multi-stage; mini-gmp is the key unlock.
smoke: HELLO.COB DISPLAY of a greeting string with STOP RUN: cobc -x -free HELLO.COB emits C, compile generated C plus libcob (built on mini-gmp) with clang.wasm to hello.wasm, run under wasmtime, expect the greeting on stdout. Second test: COMPUTE a packed-decimal PIC 9(9)V99 sum to exercise the GMP/decimal path.
blocker: libcob runtime is not a self-contained amalgam: hard GMP dependency (asm plus autotools; needs the pure-C mini-gmp substitute) plus libcob own autotools/configure build. No prebuilt wasm32-wasi artifact exists. Multi-stage port (mini-gmp then libcob then cobc-generated C) required; no codegen blocker but real build engineering. ncurses screen I/O must be stubbed.

name: Pascal (Free Pascal / FPC)
recipe: No viable lane. FPC is a self-hosting compiler written in Pascal, bootstrapped only from a native FPC binary. Its wasm32-wasi support is an OUTPUT target (it cross-compiles Pascal source to wasm); the compiler itself ships only as native binaries (x86/ARM/etc.) — no prebuilt fpc.wasm exists (Lane A fails). Not C/C++ amalgam (Lane B fails), not a Rust crate (C), not Python/JS (D). Bringing up fpc.wasm would require running the native Pascal bootstrap chain (PP=fpc cross-compile) which needs native exec — not possible in-sandbox.
smoke: N/A — no in-sandbox-runnable artifact. (Aspirational: echo 'begin writeln(42) end.' > t.pas; fpc -Twasi t.pas; wasmtime t.wasm — but fpc itself has no wasm build to run under wasmtime.)
blocker: FPC is a native self-hosting compiler; wasm32 is only an emit target, not a build for the compiler itself. No prebuilt fpc.wasm; bootstrapping requires a native FPC binary (native exec), which is unavailable in-sandbox. None of lanes A/B/C/D apply.

name: Nim
recipe: Nim transpiles to portable C, then our existing clang.wasm + wasi-libc lane takes over. Author runs `nim c --compileOnly --nimcache:out -d:release --gc:arc --os:any --threads:off <prog.nim>` (the Nim transpiler runs at authoring time, NOT in-sandbox — it's not a wasm; only its C OUTPUT ships). That emits self-contained portable C (the program plus Nim's runtime C files + nimbase.h, ~a dozen .c files against libc). Stage that nimcache C tree as a B-lane :include_only amalgam-style source set and compile all .c with clang.wasm against wasi-libc to one wasm32-wasi module. --gc:arc = deterministic refcount (no stop-the-world, no native threads); --os:any keeps it freestanding/libc-portable. C++/libc++ available if a dep needs it, but core Nim runtime is plain C.
smoke: Transpile `echo "hello from nim"; var s = 0; for i in 1..10: s += i; echo s` with `nim c --compileOnly --gc:arc --os:any --threads:off`, take the nimcache .c files, compile with clang.wasm → wasi-libc, run module under wasmtime; expect stdout `hello from nim` then `55`.
blocker: None for the language. The Nim transpiler binary is native (runs at authoring time, not in-sandbox) — only its portable C output ships through clang.wasm, so this is fine for a B-lane (pregenerated-C) toolkit. Risk: must stage the full nimcache C set (program .c + Nim runtime .c + nimbase.h) as include_only; missing any runtime .c fails the link. --gc:arc avoids any stop-the-world/thread GC concerns; native-threads must stay off (--threads:off).

name: V (vlang)
recipe: No viable lane. V is a codegen toolchain, not a droppable library. The pragmatic "V to C to clang.wasm" path requires running the V compiler to generate per-program C — but (1) the V compiler must itself be bootstrapped/compiled first (self-hosted ~100k LOC, ships a v.c bootstrap amalgam that is the compiler, links pthreads + optional boehm-GC, assumes a native host), and (2) generated C #includes the full V runtime (vlib/builtin) with heavy libc + GC/pthread deps, not a pregenerated single-file amalgam. This violates Lane B's "self-contained C, no codegen-unless-pregenerated" gate. The direct wasm backend (Lane A) is experimental, not WASI-standalone, and ships no prebuilt distributable .wasm.
smoke: N/A — no lane. (Hypothetical proof-of-life would need first compiling the V compiler bootstrap v.c under clang.wasm, which links pthreads/GC and is itself the disqualifier.)
blocker: V is a per-program codegen compiler, not a self-contained C amalgam or prebuilt wasm. Lane B requires no codegen unless pregenerated; V's C output is generated on-demand and the V compiler itself must be bootstrapped (self-hosted, links pthreads + boehm-GC, native-host assumptions). No prebuilt wasm32-wasi .wasm exists (wasm backend is experimental, non-WASI).

name: Odin
recipe: Odin is an LLVM-based compiler with a first-class `wasi_wasm32` build target (TargetMetrics target_wasi_wasm32 = {TargetOs_wasi, TargetArch_wasm32, ...}, LLVM triple wasm32-wasi) plus full WASI bindings in core:sys/wasm/wasi (65 procs, 54 types). Output runs standalone under wasmtime — no JS host, no browser, no GPU; manual memory, no mandatory GC. The compiler frontend is a self-contained C++ codebase (Lane B): build it against our live LLVM + wasm-ld (wasm-ld is the WASM linker Odin shells out to; we already have LLVM live). Wire as a compiler toolkit like the existing C/Zig/Rust lanes: `odin build prog.odin -target:wasi_wasm32` emits a wasm32-wasi module, then run under wasmtime in-sandbox. The compiler itself does NOT need to run in-sandbox for this to be useful, but porting the frontend is a nontrivial C++ build (uses our C+C++/libc++) requiring wasm-ld availability.
smoke:
printf 'package main
import "core:fmt"
main :: proc() { fmt.println("hello from odin/wasi") }
' > hello.odin && odin build hello.odin -file -target:wasi_wasm32 -out:hello.wasm && wasmtime hello.wasm  # expect: hello from odin/wasi
blocker: Odin's compiler is a large C++ codebase that must be built (Lane B) and shells out to wasm-ld for WASM linking — both LLVM and wasm-ld are already live here, so no hard blocker, but the frontend build is nontrivial vs a prebuilt drop. The wasi_wasm32 *target* itself is clean: standalone wasm32-wasi, no JS/browser/GPU. The js_wasm32 target (browser/JS-host) is out of scope; only wasi_wasm32 qualifies.

name: Roc
recipe: N/A — no viable lane. Roc is a compiler, not a droppable runtime. (A) No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi .wasm exists: Roc's wasm target is browser/JS-paired (dev-server runs apps in-browser via a JS platform) and standalone wasm requires a platform host (Rust/Zig/C) linked into the app — not a self-contained wasi CLI. (B) Compiler is Rust+Zig, not a C/C++ amalgam. (C) Large multi-crate Rust + LLVM (inkwell) + Zig — far beyond mrustc; proc-macros + LLVM + Zig all disqualify. (D) Not Python/JS. Producing Roc output needs the full LLVM+Zig toolchain (impossible in-sandbox), and running a Roc app needs a platform host that for wasm is the browser/JS pairing, not plain wasi.
smoke: None possible — no in-sandbox artifact to invoke. (Would-be: roc build app.roc --target wasm32 && wasmtime app.wasm — but this requires the LLVM+Zig compiler toolchain and a wasi platform host, neither of which exists for our lanes.)
blocker: Roc has no prebuilt standalone wasm32-wasi binary. Its wasm path is browser/JS-paired, and standalone wasm needs a platform host (Rust/Zig/C) linked into each app. Building/running Roc requires the full LLVM (inkwell) + Zig toolchain — a large multi-crate Rust project well beyond mrustc, with Zig and LLVM dependencies. No A/B/C/D lane fits.

name: Gleam
recipe: No viable lane. (A) No prebuilt plain wasm32-wasi binary: the only wasm build (gleam-wasm / compiler-wasm) is compiled for wasm32-unknown-unknown with wasm-bindgen (deps: wasm-bindgen 0.2, serde-wasm-bindgen, console_error_panic_hook, tracing-wasm) -- a browser/JS-host blob needing JS glue imports, not standalone under wasmtime. Native release binaries are OS-arch (aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu), no wasm32-wasi target. (C) The compiler is a large multi-crate Rust workspace (gleam-core + hexpm + im + serde-derive proc-macros + termcolor + camino) -- far beyond mrustc ~1.74 (proc-macro and size = impossible). (D) The brief premise that Gleam emits JS so the esbuild lane runs it conflates compiler vs output: Gleam emitted user programs are JS, but producing them requires running the Gleam compiler, which is only the wasm-bindgen browser blob (needs JS host) or the mrustc-impossible Rust workspace. No way to execute the compiler in-sandbox to get the JS. Running already-compiled Gleam-to-JS is just running JS -- the esbuild/QuickJS lane is already LIVE and adds no Gleam toolchain.
smoke: N/A -- cannot stage. The would-be smoke (gleam compile-package --target javascript then run the JS on QuickJS) is unreachable: the wasm build is wasm-bindgen (wasm32-unknown-unknown, needs a JS host, traps under bare wasmtime with no imports) and the Rust source is mrustc-impossible.
blocker: Gleam compiler's only wasm form is a wasm-bindgen wasm32-unknown-unknown browser blob requiring a JS glue host (not standalone wasm32-wasi under wasmtime); compiling from Rust source via mrustc is impossible due to the large proc-macro-heavy multi-crate workspace. The JS-emit angle only covers running Gleam output, which is plain JS already served by the LIVE esbuild/QuickJS lane and brings no Gleam toolchain in-sandbox.

name: Cython
recipe: No single-lane path. Cython itself is a large pure-Python codegen program (a Pyrex-based compiler) that requires CPython to run — it emits C. That C is not standalone: it #includes Python.h and links against the CPython C-API (PyObject, refcounting, the whole interpreter ABI). So even after our live C lane compiles the emitted .c, there is nothing to link against unless you also build/embed libpython for wasm32-wasi and run under a wasm CPython. That is the cpython.wasm/Pyodide stack, not a plain wasm32-wasi command. Our 'python' is already live, but it is the interpreter, not a libpython-dev + C-API link target for compiling arbitrary C-extensions in-sandbox. Lane A (no plain prebuilt cython.wasm exists). Lane B fails: the emitted C is not self-contained, it is glued to the CPython C-API. Lane C/D N/A (D pure-Python pip means NO C-ext; Cython's entire purpose is C-ext authoring).
smoke: In principle: cython hello.pyx -> hello.c; clang.wasm -c hello.c. Expected failure: fatal error: 'Python.h' file not found (no libpython-dev headers / C-API link target in sandbox), confirming the emitted C is not standalone.
blocker: Two-stage CPython dependency: Cython needs CPython to RUN (it's pure-Python codegen) and its output links the CPython C-API (Python.h, libpython).
